summary: Proceed only after the required edits below. The conjectural dose (C2b, V64i) is not new code. Master's decode_item (submission.py:1023-1038) and prefill's rega_lo_kernel decode_item (dfb755d3, line 2330) already order items with the chunk-within-expert index fastest, so V64i == V64, and prefill's skew loss (0.994x) was measured WITH the interleave in place. Drop V64i, and gate C2 on the reference-rebuilt judge routing, not master's zipf. As edited, this is an interpretable F1 + F2 run plus a low-odds C2 B256 candidate that its own prepare lines read out.
justification: A. F1 (w13 atomic add at T==1): measured twice on 9080a71, +2.5-3.0% at decode_1. That is roughly +0.45% on the headline, at the edge of the +-1.5% CI, but cheap and self-checked. F2 (align2 front end in _moe_wgmma): sound and well evidenced. The c05a8f73 verify_32 profile shows the 4-launch gather+cast+moe_align_block_size front end (~11.8 us) and no _align2 kernel. Master's v256 gate measured align2 at 4.70 vs 6.46 us, but at bsm 32 for Marlin; wgmma needs bsm 16, and at bsm 16/T=128 align2 LOST (0.781). So F2's own bsm-16 component gate at T=256 is required, and the spec has it. Expect -5 to -7 us of 405 us (-1.3 to -1.7%). The bitwise equivalence gate (sorted_ids[:n_padded], block_experts, n_padded, then full _moe_wgmma torch.equal) is the right strength. C2a (two CTAs/SM, NMAX 64, STG 3): the register arithmetic is right: 32x128 + 104x256 = 30720 = 80x384, and 2x30720 <= 65536. Smem fits: w2 1024 + 3x25600 + 17408 + 8192 static + 1 KB reserve = ~104.4 KB/CTA, 2 CTAs <= 228 KB. Both halves of the kernel have run on the judge: moe n64s7 at OCC1 (c30fd0cc, 168 regs, 0 spill) and prefill rega_lo at OCC2 (80 regs). But the prior evidence says C2 probably will not win at B256 under skew. Prefill measured TLP at ~0.887x on random routing and 0.994x under pop:2 skew. moe's deep-ring log shows the reference-rebuilt judge routing at T=128 has 17/32 touched experts and max 65 routes on one expert (so ~130 at T=256: 3 NMAX-64 chunks vs 2). WEAKEST LINK, C2b: the 'hot-expert tile interleave' already exists. In decode_item, cg -> (f = gf[cg], k = gk[cg]); c = f + local % k; j = local / k. Chunks of one expert are already tile-interleaved, c fastest, in master's s5 kernel, in the deep-ring kernel the hypothesis calls 'V64 (deep-ring item order)', and in prefill's rega_lo_kernel. So V64 and V64i are the same schedule. The Conjecture ('the skew loss is an ordering artefact') is already refuted by prefill's own gate, which ran with this order. The run cannot test it as written. V64 == V64i timing would read as 'L2 does not catch the duplicates' for the wrong reason. Second weak link, the gate routing: master's B256 'judge-like' routing is a calibrated zipf a=0.3 (_wg_select, submission.py:2386-2445; 457 local routes, all 32 experts touched, max ~30 routes per expert at T=256). NMAX 64 never splits a chunk under it or under random routing. So a 'worse of zipf and random' gate would see only the TLP gain and could ship V64 into the judge's hot-expert routing, where prefill says the gain vanishes. That is exactly the mis-forecast mode the caller asked about. The selector is trustworthy only if the gating set includes the reference.generate_input rebuild (_wg_judge_ids from c30fd0cc: dist normal, busiest-GPU rotation, 8 fixed-seed draws, ~17 touched experts). On trust in general: at B256 master's selector forecast the judge well (Marlin pair 497-500 vs judged 483 us, ratio 1.047-1.054x forecast vs 1.06x judged row). At B128 it did not: calibrated Marlin pair 381 vs judged 306 us (24% off), and the forced s5 B128 lost on the judge. So the gate can be trusted at B256 with the reference rebuild in the set, and cannot be trusted at B128. Expected rows: 'w13 ~239-303 / w2 ~112-148 us' does not state a gain. Master is already 239.2 / 119.0 us at bs=256. Reaching <= 385 us needs C2 to save ~13 us on top of F2. If PATH CHOSEN B256 = s5 (the likely outcome), expect verify_32 ~ -1.5% and decode_1 ~ +2.5%. Both are within or near the CI for a single run, so read attribution from the profile rows, not the headline.
confounders: align-two-phase-port-from17 (landed, a0e52640): F2 reuses its _align_two_phase/_align2_count/_align2_place kernels and extends them to the wgmma path. Its scored verify_32 '+13.4%' was measured against 9080a71 and is really the wgmma bucket's gain (align2 never ran at T=256 on the judged path). The harvest must attribute against c05a8f73 / 4e4a0e26, never 9080a71, or F2 will be credited with wgmma's win again.

cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate (on master's lineage via 40e2e860; incumbent at B256): C2's selector compares against it, and F2 changes the front end both candidates share. The selector must time master s5 WITH F2 when F2 is ON (the spec says so), or C2's ratio absorbs F2's ~6 us.

w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (landed): F1 pairs w13 atomic add with w2's atomic add at T==1. F1's two measurements were on 9080a71, which already had the w2 atomic, so this is consistent. If w2_mode falls back to master at prepare, F1's self-check tolerance still holds, but the +2.5% was never measured in that configuration.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm / triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: these set Marlin's bsm (16 at T=128, 32 at T=256) on the Marlin candidate the selector also times. They do not touch the wgmma rows, so the B256 attribution is not confounded.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m / sglang-marlin-path-parity / align-parallel-per-expert-verify: no shared launches with F1/F2/C2 on the shapes they move (the bs=256 combine is SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm in both paths). Not confounding.
interference: No companion is warranted. The three parts are separable inside one run. F1 is bs=1 only. F2 shows in the bs=256 profile as two _align2 launches replacing index_elementwise + unrolled_elementwise + moe_align_block_size_kernel + count_and_sort (~11.8 us), and C2 as wg2_kernel rows replacing wg_kernel rows. The PATH CHOSEN lines with both medians say which ran. Both a gain and a loss can be read from the profile and the prepare log without another scored run. The one question a companion could answer (does the existing c-fastest order already make L2 catch duplicate tile reads?) costs nothing extra if the V64i slot becomes a print-only de-interleaved diagnostic (V64s, chunk index slowest) timed in the same selector. A companion run would buy nothing more.
rules_flags: No per-call mutable state or process-global flag toggling is proposed. kernel_fn branches only on T and prepare-set ints (wg2_variant_256, wg_align2, W13 mode); OK under the standing policy.

Hang hazard: a setmaxnreg.inc stall is NOT bounded by the mbarrier timeout/error word, because it is a hardware stall before any mbar_wait. A hang on the judge becomes a 15-minute timeout charged to this SCORED submit. The guard (numRegs == 80 exactly, localSizeBytes == 0, occupancy >= 2, all checked by cudaFuncGetAttributes / cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor BEFORE any wg2 launch) is sufficient: per-CTA pool = numRegs x 384, and dec 32 x 128 + inc 104 x 256 balances exactly at 80. Also require: (a) static_assert(RDEC*128 + RINC*256 == REGS*THREADS) and REGS*THREADS*OCC <= 65536 in the template (prefill's GeoLo has them; port them); (b) a scan of the new module's ptxas output for any 'setmaxnreg' warning (e.g. 'ignored', 'unable to determine register count'), treated as C2 OFF, as master's _wg_ptxas_warnings does for the s5 module.

Sticky-fault hazard: the canary and self-check launch wg2 in-process, so an illegal-instruction trap kills the scored run (no child processes allowed). Today's mitigation is lineage only (the body ran at OCC1 in moe and at OCC2 in prefill). If nvcc is available on the build host, compile the new module offline for sm_90a with -Xptxas -v before submitting, and confirm 80 regs, 0 spill and no setmaxnreg warning. If it is not available, accept the risk knowingly.

The judge clones two states: wg2's grid int, its err word (int[2] with the launch marker) and any wg2 scratch must live in the state, with tensor maps encoded per call. The three-state copy check must run on the wg2 variant actually chosen, not only on s5.

Precision is unchanged: NVFP4 stays NVFP4 with register dequant, BF16 activations, fp32 accumulate. F1's atomic-add w13 changes reduction order only (self-check rel-L2 8.4e-3 <= 1e-2, well inside the judge's 1.5%).
open_questions: REQUIRED EDIT 1: drop V64i as a 'new interleave'. It is master's existing decode_item order. Either remove the candidate, or replace it with a print-only V64s (c slowest: item -> (expert group, chunk, tile)) timed under the reference-rebuilt routing. V64s vs V64 then measures what the existing interleave already buys from L2 and actually tests the Conjecture's mechanism. Rewrite the Conjecture to the testable claim: 'OCC2 TLP at NMAX 64 survives the judge's hot-expert split at B256'.

REQUIRED EDIT 2: C2's gating routings must include the reference.generate_input rebuild (_wg_judge_ids, ported from c30fd0cc, fixed CPU seed, touched-expert count printed). Master has no such routing: its 'judge-like' is a zipf a=0.3 with all 32 experts touched, and NMAX 64 never splits under it. Gate = worse of {reference rebuild, zipf a=0.3}, with random printed only. Print chunk count and 'weight read twice' MB per candidate per routing, and assert the chosen candidate is the fastest printed on the gating routing.

REQUIRED EDIT 3: make B128 print-only for C2: never enabled from this run. The B128 forecast is untrustworthy (calibrated Marlin pair 381 vs judged 306 us; forced s5 lost on the judge). Prior B128 wgmma variants sat at 0.80-0.81x of Marlin, and ~11% TLP cannot reach the 1.02x gate. B128 is also the scope of queued wg-two-ctas-per-sm-port-b128-n32, so do not pre-empt it.

Selector multiple-comparison bias: picking the min of {s5, V64} (plus a diagnostic) at a 0.98 margin on 41 reps is mild winner's curse. B256's forecast error has been ~1-3%, so keep 0.98 but require the win on BOTH gating routings, as written.

Does nvcc exist on this workstation for an offline sm_90a compile of the new module (no GPU needed)? That is the only pre-submit check available for the numRegs == 80 / no-spill / setmaxnreg-warning conditions.

Fix the expected rows: master is already at w13 239.2 / w2 119.0 us at bs=256, so 'w13 ~239-303 / w2 ~112-148' is not a gain. State the C2 target as w13+w2 <= ~345 us (-13 us) if V64 is chosen. Otherwise verify_32 is expected to be F2 alone (~ -1.5%).

If C2 loses under the reference rebuild, as prefill predicts, the follow-up that could make two CTAs pay under skew is w13 at OCC2 with NMAX 128 and STG 2 (1024 + 2x41984 + 18432 + 8192 + 1024 ~ 110 KB/CTA, fits 2/SM; w2's 34816-B epilogue does not fit). That keeps hot experts in 2 chunks and is worth a separate hypothesis, not part of this run.
